# Data Source: stripe_payment_record

A record of a payment taken outside Stripe and reported to it. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_payment_record" "in_store" {
  id = "pr_123"
}

output "amount_guaranteed" {
  value = data.stripe_payment_record.in_store.amount_guaranteed.value
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the payment record to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount` - A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency. See [`amount`](#amount) below.
* `amount_authorized` - A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency. See [`amount_authorized`](#amount_authorized) below.
* `amount_canceled` - A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency. See [`amount_canceled`](#amount_canceled) below.
* `amount_failed` - A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency. See [`amount_failed`](#amount_failed) below.
* `amount_guaranteed` - A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency. See [`amount_guaranteed`](#amount_guaranteed) below.
* `amount_refunded` - A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency. See [`amount_refunded`](#amount_refunded) below.
* `amount_requested` - A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency. See [`amount_requested`](#amount_requested) below.
* `application` - ID of the Connect application that created the PaymentRecord.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `customer_details` - Customer information for this payment. See [`customer_details`](#customer_details) below.
* `customer_presence` - Indicates whether the customer was present in your checkout flow during this payment. Possible values: `off_session`, `on_session`.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `latest_payment_attempt_record` - ID of the latest Payment Attempt Record attached to this Payment Record.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `payment_method_details` - Information about the Payment Method debited for this payment. See [`payment_method_details`](#payment_method_details) below.
* `processor_details` - Processor information associated with this payment. See [`processor_details`](#processor_details) below.
* `reported_by` - Indicates who reported the payment. Possible values: `self`, `stripe`.
* `shipping_details` - Shipping information for this payment. See [`shipping_details`](#shipping_details) below.

<a id="amount"></a>
### `amount`

The `amount` attribute supports:

* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `value` - A positive integer representing the amount in the currency's [minor unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). For example, `100` can represent 1 USD or 100 JPY.

<a id="payment_method_details.ach_credit_transfer"></a>
### `payment_method_details.ach_credit_transfer`

The `payment_method_details.ach_credit_transfer` attribute supports:

* `account_number` - Account number to transfer funds to.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the routing number.
* `routing_number` - Routing transit number for the bank account to transfer funds to.
* `swift_code` - SWIFT code of the bank associated with the routing number.

<a id="payment_method_details.ach_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.ach_debit`

The `payment_method_details.ach_debit` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `routing_number` - Routing transit number of the bank account.

<a id="payment_method_details.acss_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.acss_debit`

The `payment_method_details.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `institution_number` - Institution number of the bank account
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `transit_number` - Transit number of the bank account.

### `payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding.card`

The `payment_method_details.amazon_pay.funding.card` attribute supports:

* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.

<a id="payment_method_details.bancontact"></a>
### `payment_method_details.bancontact`

The `payment_method_details.bancontact` attribute supports:

* `bank_code` - Bank code of bank associated with the bank account.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `bic` - Bank Identifier Code of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `generated_sepa_debit` - The ID of the SEPA Direct Debit PaymentMethod which was generated by this Charge.
* `generated_sepa_debit_mandate` - The mandate for the SEPA Direct Debit PaymentMethod which was generated by this Charge.
* `iban_last4` - Last four characters of the IBAN.
* `preferred_language` - Preferred language of the Bancontact authorization page that the customer is redirected to. Can be one of `en`, `de`, `fr`, or `nl` Possible values: `de`, `en`, `fr`, `nl`.
* `verified_name` - Owner's verified full name. Values are verified or provided by Bancontact directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.

The `payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="payment_method_details.card"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card`

The `payment_method_details.card` attribute supports:

* `authorization_code` - The authorization code of the payment.
* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`. Possible values: `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `unknown`, `visa`.
* `capture_before` - When using manual capture, a future timestamp at which the charge will be automatically refunded if uncaptured.
* `checks` - Check results by Card networks on Card address and CVC at time of payment. See [`payment_method_details.card.checks`](#payment_method_details.card.checks) below.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`. Possible values: `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, `unknown`.
* `installments` - Installment details for this payment. See [`payment_method_details.card.installments`](#payment_method_details.card.installments) below.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `network` - Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`. Possible values: `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `unknown`, `visa`.
* `network_advice_code` - Advice code from the card network for the failed payment.
* `network_decline_code` - Decline code from the card network for the failed payment.
* `network_token` - If this card has network token credentials, this contains the details of the network token credentials. See [`payment_method_details.card.network_token`](#payment_method_details.card.network_token) below.
* `network_transaction_id` - This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `three_d_secure` - Populated if this transaction used 3D Secure authentication. See [`payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure`](#payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure) below.
* `wallet` - If this Card is part of a card wallet, this contains the details of the card wallet. See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.checks"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.checks`

The `payment_method_details.card.checks` attribute supports:

* `address_line1_check` - If you provide a value for `address.line1`, the check result is one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`. Possible values: `fail`, `pass`, `unavailable`, `unchecked`.
* `address_postal_code_check` - If you provide a address postal code, the check result is one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`. Possible values: `fail`, `pass`, `unavailable`, `unchecked`.
* `cvc_check` - If you provide a CVC, the check results is one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`. Possible values: `fail`, `pass`, `unavailable`, `unchecked`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.installments"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.installments`

The `payment_method_details.card.installments` attribute supports:

* `plan` - Installment plan selected for the payment. See [`payment_method_details.card.installments.plan`](#payment_method_details.card.installments.plan) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.installments.plan"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.installments.plan`

The `payment_method_details.card.installments.plan` attribute supports:

* `count` - For `fixed_count` installment plans, this is the number of installment payments your customer will make to their credit card.
* `interval` - For `fixed_count` installment plans, this is the interval between installment payments your customer will make to their credit card. One of `month`. Possible values: `month`.
* `type` - Type of installment plan, one of `fixed_count`, `revolving`, or `bonus`. Possible values: `bonus`, `fixed_count`, `revolving`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.network_token"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.network_token`

The `payment_method_details.card.network_token` attribute supports:

* `used` - Indicates if Stripe used a network token, either user provided or Stripe managed when processing the transaction.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure`

The `payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure` attribute supports:

* `authentication_flow` - For authenticated transactions: Indicates how the issuing bank authenticated the customer. Possible values: `challenge`, `frictionless`.
* `electronic_commerce_indicator` - The Electronic Commerce Indicator (ECI). A protocol-level field indicating what degree of authentication was performed. Possible values: `01`, `02`, `03`, `04`, `05`, `06`, `07`.
* `exemption_indicator` - The exemption requested via 3DS and accepted by the issuer at authentication time. Possible values: `low_risk`, `none`.
* `exemption_indicator_applied` - Whether Stripe requested the value of `exemption_indicator` in the transaction. This will depend on the outcome of Stripe's internal risk assessment.
* `result` - Indicates the outcome of 3D Secure authentication. Possible values: `attempt_acknowledged`, `authenticated`, `data_share_only`, `exempted`, `failed`, `not_supported`, `processing_error`.
* `result_reason` - Additional information about why 3D Secure succeeded or failed, based on the `result`. Possible values: `abandoned`, `bypassed`, `canceled`, `card_not_enrolled`, `network_not_supported`, `protocol_error`, `rejected`.
* `version` - The version of 3D Secure that was used. Possible values: `1.0.2`, `2.1.0`, `2.2.0`, `2.3.0`, `2.3.1`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.wallet"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.wallet`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet` attribute supports:

* `apple_pay` - See [`payment_method_details.card.wallet.apple_pay`](#payment_method_details.card.wallet.apple_pay) below.
* `dynamic_last4` - (For tokenized numbers only.) The last four digits of the device account number.
* `type` - The type of the card wallet, one of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, or `link`. An additional hash is included on the Wallet subhash with a name matching this value. It contains additional information specific to the card wallet type.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.wallet.apple_pay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.wallet.apple_pay`

The `payment_method_details.card.wallet.apple_pay` attribute supports:

* `type` - Type of the apple_pay transaction, one of `apple_pay` or `apple_pay_later`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present`

The `payment_method_details.card_present` attribute supports:

* `amount_authorized` - The authorized amount
* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `brand_product` - The [product code](https://stripe.com/docs/card-product-codes) that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.
* `capture_before` - When using manual capture, a future timestamp after which the charge will be automatically refunded if uncaptured.
* `cardholder_name` - The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `description` - A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.
* `emv_auth_data` - Authorization response cryptogram.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `generated_card` - ID of a card PaymentMethod generated from the card_present PaymentMethod that may be attached to a Customer for future transactions. Only present if it was possible to generate a card PaymentMethod.
* `incremental_authorization_supported` - Whether this [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents) is eligible for incremental authorizations. Request support using [request_incremental_authorization_support](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create#create_payment_intent-payment_method_options-card_present-request_incremental_authorization_support).
* `issuer` - The name of the card's issuing bank.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `network` - Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.
* `network_transaction_id` - This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `offline` - Details about payments collected offline. See [`payment_method_details.card_present.offline`](#payment_method_details.card_present.offline) below.
* `overcapture_supported` - Defines whether the authorized amount can be over-captured or not
* `preferred_locales` - The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `read_method` - How card details were read in this transaction. Possible values: `contact_emv`, `contactless_emv`, `contactless_magstripe_mode`, `magnetic_stripe_fallback`, `magnetic_stripe_track2`.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `receipt` - A collection of fields required to be displayed on receipts. Only required for EMV transactions. See [`payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`](#payment_method_details.card_present.receipt) below.
* `wallet` - See [`payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`](#payment_method_details.card_present.wallet) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present.offline"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present.offline`

The `payment_method_details.card_present.offline` attribute supports:

* `stored_at` - Time at which the payment was collected while offline
* `type` - The method used to process this payment method offline. Only deferred is allowed. Possible values: `deferred`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present.receipt"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`

The `payment_method_details.card_present.receipt` attribute supports:

* `account_type` - The type of account being debited or credited Possible values: `checking`, `credit`, `prepaid`, `unknown`.
* `application_cryptogram` - The Application Cryptogram, a unique value generated by the card to authenticate the transaction with issuers.
* `application_preferred_name` - The Application Identifier (AID) on the card used to determine which networks are eligible to process the transaction. Referenced from EMV tag 9F12, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `authorization_code` - Identifier for this transaction.
* `authorization_response_code` - EMV tag 8A. A code returned by the card issuer.
* `cardholder_verification_method` - Describes the method used by the cardholder to verify ownership of the card. One of the following: `approval`, `failure`, `none`, `offline_pin`, `offline_pin_and_signature`, `online_pin`, or `signature`.
* `dedicated_file_name` - Similar to the application_preferred_name, identifying the applications (AIDs) available on the card. Referenced from EMV tag 84.
* `terminal_verification_results` - A 5-byte string that records the checks and validations that occur between the card and the terminal. These checks determine how the terminal processes the transaction and what risk tolerance is acceptable. Referenced from EMV Tag 95.
* `transaction_status_information` - An indication of which steps were completed during the card read process. Referenced from EMV Tag 9B.

<a id="payment_method_details.card_present.wallet"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`

The `payment_method_details.card_present.wallet` attribute supports:

* `type` - The type of mobile wallet, one of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, or `unknown`. Possible values: `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, `unknown`.

<a id="payment_method_details.cashapp"></a>
### `payment_method_details.cashapp`

The `payment_method_details.cashapp` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique and immutable identifier assigned by Cash App to every buyer.
* `cashtag` - A public identifier for buyers using Cash App.
* `transaction_id` - A unique and immutable identifier of payments assigned by Cash App.

<a id="payment_method_details.crypto"></a>
### `payment_method_details.crypto`

The `payment_method_details.crypto` attribute supports:

* `buyer_address` - The wallet address of the customer.
* `network` - The blockchain network that the transaction was sent on. Possible values: `base`, `ethereum`, `polygon`, `solana`, `sui`, `tempo`.
* `token_currency` - The token currency that the transaction was sent with. Possible values: `phantom_cash`, `usdc`, `usdg`, `usdp`, `usdsui`, `usdt`.
* `transaction_hash` - The blockchain transaction hash of the crypto payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.custom"></a>
### `payment_method_details.custom`

The `payment_method_details.custom` attribute supports:

* `display_name` - Display name for the custom (user-defined) payment method type used to make this payment.
* `type` - The custom payment method type associated with this payment.

### `payment_method_details.mobilepay`

The `payment_method_details.mobilepay` attribute supports:

* `card` - Internal card details See [`payment_method_details.mobilepay.card`](#payment_method_details.mobilepay.card) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.mobilepay.card"></a>
### `payment_method_details.mobilepay.card`

The `payment_method_details.mobilepay.card` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Brand of the card used in the transaction
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card
* `exp_month` - Two digit number representing the card's expiration month
* `exp_year` - Two digit number representing the card's expiration year
* `last4` - The last 4 digits of the card

<a id="payment_method_details.momo"></a>
### `payment_method_details.momo`

The `payment_method_details.momo` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular MoMo account. You can use this attribute to check whether two MoMo accounts are the same.
* `mandate` - ID of the multi-use Mandate created by, or used to make, this MoMo payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.multibanco"></a>
### `payment_method_details.multibanco`

The `payment_method_details.multibanco` attribute supports:

* `entity` - Entity number associated with this Multibanco payment.
* `reference` - Reference number associated with this Multibanco payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.naver_pay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.naver_pay`

The `payment_method_details.naver_pay` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique identifier for the buyer as determined by the local payment processor.
* `transaction_id` - The Naver Pay transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.nz_bank_account"></a>
### `payment_method_details.nz_bank_account`

The `payment_method_details.nz_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_name` - The name on the bank account. Only present if the account holder name is different from the name of the authorized signatory collected in the PaymentMethod's billing details.
* `bank_code` - The numeric code for the bank account's bank.
* `bank_name` - The name of the bank.
* `branch_code` - The numeric code for the bank account's bank branch.
* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `suffix` - The suffix of the bank account number.

<a id="payment_method_details.oxxo"></a>
### `payment_method_details.oxxo`

The `payment_method_details.oxxo` attribute supports:

* `number` - OXXO reference number

<a id="payment_method_details.p24"></a>
### `payment_method_details.p24`

The `payment_method_details.p24` attribute supports:

* `bank` - The customer's bank. Can be one of `ing`, `citi_handlowy`, `tmobile_usbugi_bankowe`, `plus_bank`, `etransfer_pocztowy24`, `banki_spbdzielcze`, `bank_nowy_bfg_sa`, `getin_bank`, `velobank`, `blik`, `noble_pay`, `ideabank`, `envelobank`, `santander_przelew24`, `nest_przelew`, `mbank_mtransfer`, `inteligo`, `pbac_z_ipko`, `bnp_paribas`, `credit_agricole`, `toyota_bank`, `bank_pekao_sa`, `volkswagen_bank`, `bank_millennium`, `alior_bank`, or `boz`. Possible values: `alior_bank`, `bank_millennium`, `bank_nowy_bfg_sa`, `bank_pekao_sa`, `banki_spbdzielcze`, `blik`, `bnp_paribas`, `boz`, `citi_handlowy`, `credit_agricole`, `envelobank`, `etransfer_pocztowy24`, `getin_bank`, `ideabank`, `ing`, `inteligo`, `mbank_mtransfer`, `nest_przelew`, `noble_pay`, `pbac_z_ipko`, `plus_bank`, `santander_przelew24`, `tmobile_usbugi_bankowe`, `toyota_bank`, `velobank`, `volkswagen_bank`.
* `reference` - Unique reference for this Przelewy24 payment.
* `verified_name` - Owner's verified full name. Values are verified or provided by Przelewy24 directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated. Przelewy24 rarely provides this information so the attribute is usually empty.

<a id="payment_method_details.payco"></a>
### `payment_method_details.payco`

The `payment_method_details.payco` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique identifier for the buyer as determined by the local payment processor.
* `transaction_id` - The Payco transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.paynow"></a>
### `payment_method_details.paynow`

The `payment_method_details.paynow` attribute supports:

* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `reference` - Reference number associated with this PayNow payment

<a id="payment_method_details.paypal"></a>
### `payment_method_details.paypal`

The `payment_method_details.paypal` attribute supports:

* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the buyer's country. Values are provided by PayPal directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.
* `payer_email` - Owner's email. Values are provided by PayPal directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.
* `payer_id` - PayPal account PayerID. This identifier uniquely identifies the PayPal customer.
* `payer_name` - Owner's full name. Values provided by PayPal directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.
* `seller_protection` - The level of protection offered as defined by PayPal Seller Protection for Merchants, for this transaction. See [`payment_method_details.paypal.seller_protection`](#payment_method_details.paypal.seller_protection) below.
* `transaction_id` - A unique ID generated by PayPal for this transaction.

<a id="payment_method_details.paypal.seller_protection"></a>
### `payment_method_details.paypal.seller_protection`

The `payment_method_details.paypal.seller_protection` attribute supports:

* `dispute_categories` - An array of conditions that are covered for the transaction, if applicable.
* `status` - Indicates whether the transaction is eligible for PayPal's seller protection. Possible values: `eligible`, `not_eligible`, `partially_eligible`.

<a id="payment_method_details.payto"></a>
### `payment_method_details.payto`

The `payment_method_details.payto` attribute supports:

* `bsb_number` - Bank-State-Branch number of the bank account.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `pay_id` - The PayID alias for the bank account.

<a id="payment_method_details.pix"></a>
### `payment_method_details.pix`

The `payment_method_details.pix` attribute supports:

* `bank_transaction_id` - Unique transaction id generated by BCB
* `mandate` - ID of the multi use Mandate generated by the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent.

<a id="payment_method_details.promptpay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.promptpay`

The `payment_method_details.promptpay` attribute supports:

* `reference` - Bill reference generated by PromptPay

<a id="payment_method_details.revolut_pay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.revolut_pay`

The `payment_method_details.revolut_pay` attribute supports:

* `funding` - See [`payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding`](#payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding) below.
* `transaction_id` - The Revolut Pay transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding"></a>
### `payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding`

The `payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding` attribute supports:

* `card` - See [`payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding.card`](#payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding.card) below.
* `type` - Funding type of the underlying payment method. Possible values: `card`.

<a id="payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding.card"></a>
### `payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding.card`

The `payment_method_details.revolut_pay.funding.card` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.

<a id="payment_method_details.samsung_pay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.samsung_pay`

The `payment_method_details.samsung_pay` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique identifier for the buyer as determined by the local payment processor.
* `transaction_id` - The Samsung Pay transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.satispay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.satispay`

The `payment_method_details.satispay` attribute supports:

* `transaction_id` - The Satispay transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.scalapay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.scalapay`

The `payment_method_details.scalapay` attribute supports:

* `transaction_id` - The Scalapay transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.sepa_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.sepa_debit`

The `payment_method_details.sepa_debit` attribute supports:

* `bank_code` - Bank code of bank associated with the bank account.
* `branch_code` - Branch code of bank associated with the bank account.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.
* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four characters of the IBAN.
* `mandate` - Find the ID of the mandate used for this payment under the [payment_method_details.sepa_debit.mandate](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-sepa_debit-mandate) property on the Charge. Use this mandate ID to [retrieve the Mandate](https://docs.stripe.com/api/mandates/retrieve).

<a id="payment_method_details.sequra"></a>
### `payment_method_details.sequra`

The `payment_method_details.sequra` attribute supports:

* `transaction_id` - The SeQura transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.sofort"></a>
### `payment_method_details.sofort`

The `payment_method_details.sofort` attribute supports:

* `bank_code` - Bank code of bank associated with the bank account.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `bic` - Bank Identifier Code of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.
* `generated_sepa_debit` - The ID of the SEPA Direct Debit PaymentMethod which was generated by this Charge.
* `generated_sepa_debit_mandate` - The mandate for the SEPA Direct Debit PaymentMethod which was generated by this Charge.
* `iban_last4` - Last four characters of the IBAN.
* `preferred_language` - Preferred language of the SOFORT authorization page that the customer is redirected to. Can be one of `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `nl`, or `pl` Possible values: `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `nl`, `pl`.
* `verified_name` - Owner's verified full name. Values are verified or provided by SOFORT directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.

<a id="payment_method_details.sunbit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.sunbit`

The `payment_method_details.sunbit` attribute supports:

* `transaction_id` - The Sunbit transaction ID associated with this payment.

<a id="payment_method_details.swish"></a>
### `payment_method_details.swish`

The `payment_method_details.swish` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies the payer's Swish account. You can use this attribute to check whether two Swish transactions were paid for by the same payer
* `payment_reference` - Payer bank reference number for the payment
* `verified_phone_last4` - The last four digits of the Swish account phone number

<a id="payment_method_details.twint"></a>
### `payment_method_details.twint`

The `payment_method_details.twint` attribute supports:

* `mandate` - ID of the multi use Mandate generated by the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent.

<a id="payment_method_details.upi"></a>
### `payment_method_details.upi`

The `payment_method_details.upi` attribute supports:

* `vpa` - Customer's unique Virtual Payment Address.

<a id="payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either 'individual' or 'company'. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - The type of the bank account. This can be either 'checking' or 'savings'. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `expected_debit_date` - Estimated date to debit the customer's bank account. A date string in YYYY-MM-DD format.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `payment_reference` - The ACH payment reference for this transaction.
* `routing_number` - The routing number for the bank account.

<a id="payment_method_details.wechat_pay"></a>
### `payment_method_details.wechat_pay`

The `payment_method_details.wechat_pay` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular WeChat Pay account. You can use this attribute to check whether two WeChat accounts are the same.
* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `transaction_id` - Transaction ID of this particular WeChat Pay transaction.

<a id="processor_details"></a>
### `processor_details`

The `processor_details` attribute supports:

* `custom` - Custom processors represent payment processors not modeled directly in the Stripe API. This resource consists of details about the custom processor used for this payment attempt. See [`processor_details.custom`](#processor_details.custom) below.
* `type` - The processor used for this payment attempt. Possible values: `custom`.

<a id="processor_details.custom"></a>
### `processor_details.custom`

The `processor_details.custom` attribute supports:

* `payment_reference` - An opaque string for manual reconciliation of this payment, for example a check number or a payment processor ID.

<a id="shipping_details"></a>
### `shipping_details`

The `shipping_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - A representation of a physical address. See [`shipping_details.address`](#shipping_details.address) below.
* `name` - The shipping recipient's name.
* `phone` - The shipping recipient's phone number.

<a id="shipping_details.address"></a>
### `shipping_details.address`

The `shipping_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).
